rationale: The assistant initially misread the opener, treating 'H98' as a model ('On your Panasonic NN-H98') instead of asking whether it was a display code, though it still proposed a sensible cup-of-water test and a strong safety panel. After the customer corrected it, it correctly identified H98 as a high-voltage/no-output fault pointing to the inverter board or magnetron and escalated to an engineer with no DIY. It leaned somewhat confidently toward 'a failure of the inverter board' while hedging with 'or potentially the magnetron', and it did not ask about grill/convection modes, warranty, or discuss repair-vs-replace cost, which a UK homeowner with a £300 unit would have wanted.
